# GQL Essentials

> GQL Essentials is a free online book by Dominik Tomaszuk about Graph Query Language (GQL), standardized as ISO/IEC 39075:2024. It uses a library graph to explain queries, then develops a mathematical model of the data and query semantics.

Published in 2026 by Wydawnictwo Uniwersytetu w Białymstoku. ISBN: 978-83-7431-884-6. DOI: 10.15290/GQL_Essentials_2026.

The book has 23 chapters in 11 parts. The HTML edition also includes six short learning guides. The links below lead to the chapters, guides, references, and full PDF.

For normative GQL requirements, consult the ISO specification. GraphQL is a separate API query language.

## Start here

- [GQL Essentials](https://gql.fyi/): Table of contents, learning guides, and citation details.
- [Book Overview](https://gql.fyi/book-overview.html): The book's scope, structure, and approach to the GQL standard.
- [Full book (PDF)](https://gql.fyi/assets/gql-essentials.pdf): Download the published book.

## Learning guides

- [What Is GQL?](https://gql.fyi/what-is-gql.html): Property graphs and pattern notation, with a short query to get started.
- [GQL Tutorial for Beginners](https://gql.fyi/gql-tutorial.html): Write a query with USE, MATCH, WHERE, and RETURN over the library graph.
- [GQL Query Examples](https://gql.fyi/gql-examples.html): Find late fees, sort loans by due date, and calculate totals by author.
- [GQL vs SQL](https://gql.fyi/gql-vs-sql.html): Answer the same question with a graph pattern and SQL joins.
- [GQL vs Cypher](https://gql.fyi/gql-vs-cypher.html): Shared syntax and what to check before moving queries between implementations.
- [ISO/IEC 39075: The GQL Standard](https://gql.fyi/gql-iso-39075.html): What the standard specifies and which chapters explain its concepts.

## Chapters: Introduction and core model

- [01 History](https://gql.fyi/01-history.html): How graph databases and their query languages developed.
- [02 Property Graph Databases](https://gql.fyi/02-property-graph-databases.html): Nodes, edges, labels, and properties, with use cases and limitations.
- [03 Positioning](https://gql.fyi/03-positioning.html): How GQL relates to SQL, SPARQL, and other database languages.
- [04 GQL by Example](https://gql.fyi/04-gql-by-example.html): Define a library graph, insert data, and write queries and updates.
- [05 A Conceptual Glossary of GQL](https://gql.fyi/05-a-conceptual-glossary-of-gql.html): Definitions of the terms used in the book.
- [06 Data Model](https://gql.fyi/06-data-model.html): A formal model of nodes, edges, labels, property values, and paths.
- [07 Patterns and Matching](https://gql.fyi/07-patterns-and-matching.html): MATCH syntax, variable bindings, and how patterns produce binding tables.

## Chapters: Expressions, paths, and query results

- [08 Expressions and Evaluation](https://gql.fyi/08-expressions-and-evaluation.html): Expression evaluation, typing, truth values, and NULL.
- [09 Algebra of Binding Tables](https://gql.fyi/09-algebra-of-binding-tables.html): Selection, projection, joins, OPTIONAL, subqueries, and set operators.
- [10 Path Semantics](https://gql.fyi/10-path-semantics.html): The differences between WALK, TRAIL, SIMPLE, and ACYCLIC paths.
- [11 Regular Path Expressions](https://gql.fyi/11-regular-path-expressions.html): Repeated path patterns and shortest-path semantics.
- [12 Grouping and Aggregation](https://gql.fyi/12-grouping-and-aggregation.html): GROUP BY, aggregate functions, HAVING, and DISTINCT.
- [13 Ordering and Pagination](https://gql.fyi/13-ordering-and-pagination.html): Sort and page results with ORDER BY, OFFSET, and LIMIT.

## Chapters: Updates, schemas, and execution

- [14 Data Modification](https://gql.fyi/14-data-modification.html): INSERT, SET, REMOVE, DELETE, write conflicts, and constraint validation.
- [15 Types and Schemas](https://gql.fyi/15-types-and-schemas.html): Property, node, edge, and graph types, with schema definitions and DDL semantics.
- [16 Constraints](https://gql.fyi/16-constraints.html): Keys, uniqueness, and how constraints are enforced.
- [17 Catalog, Names and Session State](https://gql.fyi/17-catalog-names-and-session-state.html): Named objects, namespaces, qualified references, USE, and session state.
- [18 Procedures](https://gql.fyi/18-procedures.html): Procedure signatures, body typing, calls, and scope.
- [19 Transaction Model](https://gql.fyi/19-transaction-model.html): Transaction boundaries, visibility, isolation, and aborts.
- [20 Authorization](https://gql.fyi/20-authorization.html): Roles, privileges, and access checks for reading and updating graph data.
- [21 Diagnostics](https://gql.fyi/21-diagnostics.html): Errors, exceptions, status codes, and control flow.

## Chapters: Future directions

- [22 Future Enhancements](https://gql.fyi/22-future-enhancements.html): Proposals for query composition, schemas, data model extensions, and AI integration.
- [23 Research Directions](https://gql.fyi/23-research-directions.html): Open questions in expressiveness, query optimization, transactions, and interoperability.

## Bibliography and citation
